source.title: Antibody: Strengthening Defense Against Harmful Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models via Attenuating Harmful Gradient Influence
source.authors: Q. Nguyen; T. Le; Jing Wu; A. Bui; Mehrtash Harandi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies fine-tuning with harmful examples mixed into task data and measures harmful responses, but uses Harmful Score rather than refusal rate and does not reproduce the original studies’ full methods.
record.gate_note: The paper's statements about prior studies, including that harmful fine-tuning can compromise safety, are cited background and not extracted as results. Table 3 reports harmful-score results at multiple harmful-data ratios; Table 1 and Table 2 report additional task and model settings. The paper also describes Figure 1 as showing safety degradation with increasing sample size at a fixed 20% harmful ratio, but does not state the figure's exact values.
record.test_reason: The paper is a defense study, but its undefended SFT baseline reports Harmful Score after fine-tuning on task data with 0–25% harmful examples. That bears on V1. The harmful-ratio sweep includes a clean (benign-only) arm, so the dose-response can be read against a matched control.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that Antibody (flatness-regularized alignment plus refusal-likelihood sample weighting) mitigates harmful fine-tuning while keeping task accuracy. They also acknowledge computational cost and weakness at large learning rates.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses mixed benign-task and harmful-compliance fine-tuning, then evaluates Harmful Score rather than refusal rate. It studies defense methods and does not reproduce the original sources' full protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported SFT harmful score changes across harmful ratios. Figure 1 describes safety degradation as sample size increases at a fixed 20% harmful ratio. The paper also reports model- and task-dependent outcomes.
record.problems: Harmful Score is a moderation-model flag rate, not a direct refusal rate. Matched no-fine-tuning baselines are not reported for the Table 1 and Table 2 SFT results, and the clean GSM8K score does not provide a pre-fine-tuning reference. Most results are averages over three seeds without reported error bars; AlpacaEval uses one seed. Figure 1 has no exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 Fine-tuning Accuracy values are not safety/compliance measures. Comparator-method Harmful Score values at p > 0 are not included as rows because those methods are defenses rather than unprotected fine-tuning tests; their clean-condition controls and fine-tuning-task results are also omitted. Tables 1 and 2 rows for other methods are omitted for the same reason. Figure 3 reports defense performance over epochs and learning rates, not the unprotected SFT effect measured by V1.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on harmful-only data. Full-parameter fine-tuning (only LoRA, lr 1e-5, is used). Refusal-rate measures. Pre-fine-tuning reference scores.
Whether benign-only fine-tuning raises harmful compliance. Only the post-fine-tuning clean HS (2.05) is given, with no pre-fine-tuning score.

missing.what: SFT-baseline Harmful Score on other tasks for Qwen-2-7B: SST2 33.86, AGNEWS 31.00. For Gemma-2-9B: SST2 40.77, AGNEWS 39.91. All at default p=0.2.
Corrected Table 3 SFT row: clean HS 2.05; p=0.05 10.68; 0.1 15.59; 0.15 19.06; 0.2 23.94; 0.25 27.85. The 12.23 value belongs to the FA clean column.

record.verdict_notes: The main extraction error is a one-column shift in Table 3. The HS block has 8 values under 7 headers, because the first FA value (12.23) was parsed into it. The shift is confirmed by the row averages and by the p=0.2 match with Tables 1 and 2. With the correct values, the 'reversed' states vanish and V1 shows a clean dose-response from a low baseline. The safety alignment is the authors' own SFT alignment stage with LoRA, not the vendor chat model, which matters when comparing with the originals.

versions.untested_parts: It tests mixed benign-and-harmful task fine-tuning, not fine-tuning using only harmful examples. The harmful response measure is Harmful Score, not refusal rate.
A benign-only condition is measured, but no unfine-tuned or otherwise matched baseline is reported to establish whether benign fine-tuning raised harmful compliance.
No per-token KL or aligned-versus-base output-distribution comparison.
No compliant-opening prefills, suffix attacks, or decoding changes.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The paper proposes a defense mechanism but does not test whether the data or training objective causes safety shallowness.
No training designed to spread safety across response tokens or evaluation of whether such deepening holds up.
